validity.recommendation: Check start year (1986 per Ukrainian Wikipedia, 1968 on sheet) and capacity (20 per two sources, 23.7 on sheet).
validity.researcher_notes: The line exists. A 2009 Naftogaz plan names it and Ukrainian Wikipedia has a dedicated article: 1200 mm, commissioned 1986, capacity raised to 20 bcm per year after 2001. Moldovatransgaz lists the Moldovan part as 62.91 km, 1220 mm, 20 bcm per year. The sheet shows start year 1968 and capacity 23.7, and I found support for neither. It is not a duplicate of P0784 or P1481 on documents.

fills.researcher_notes: Ukrainian Wikipedia describes the line in the present tense as the main southern transit route. The 2009 Naftogaz plan treats it as a live line to modernize. Neither is dated 2024 or later, so the status is medium. No source says it is idle.

Ukrainian Wikipedia says the 1200 mm line was commissioned in 1986, together with the Anan'iv compressor station, and the Tiraspol-2 station started two years later. That conflicts with 1968 on the sheet. The 1968 may be a typo for 1986. I did not stage a change on one source. Flagged as a spec concern.

fills.researcher_notes: Ukrainian Wikipedia and Moldovatransgaz both give 20 bcm per year. The sheet has 23.7. I found no source for 23.7 that I could open; an earlier read of the 2017 KPMG report found no such figure for this line. Proposing 20 per the two agreeing sources. Old value was 23.70.

The 2017 KPMG report, which an earlier pass read, gives 257 km, and English Wikipedia gives 256 km. Neither page could be opened and checked today because the web archive was offline and the KPMG host refused the connection. Moldovatransgaz gives only the Moldovan part, 62.91 km. Value kept as is.
Ukrainian Wikipedia's article on this line gives 1200 mm. Moldovatransgaz lists it as 1220 mm, which is likely the outer diameter of the same pipe. The sheet value stands.

fills.researcher_notes: Ukrainian Wikipedia says the line starts at the Anan'iv compressor station and ends near Izmail. The start location is blank on the sheet, so Anan'iv is offered as a fill. The line also crosses Moldova and Transnistria.

Searched for a construction cost. The 2017 KPMG report, read in an earlier pass, lists a net book value of 41 million dollars, which is an accounting value and not a build cost. Nothing else found. Value kept, unsupported.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This line exits to Romania near Orlivka. A December 2025 Amber Grid presentation shows reverse flows from Romania through Orlivka-Isaccea in 2025, so the southern end is in use. It does not name the line. Russian transit ended on 1 January 2025. Kept as operating, covering the Ukrainian section only.

summary: "Real; start year 1986 vs sheet 1968 and capacity 20 vs 23.7 contested; length/cost/owner unresolved"
